For antiferromagnetic Ising-like and XY-like models of spin j-particles living on a complete graph, the energy minimum for symmetric separable states is given with the expectation value of single-particle operators. For the ferromagnetic Heisenberg chain of spin-1/2 particles, the minimum is expressed via the Uhlmann-Jozsa fidelity. These relations enable the extraction of the quantum Fisher information and quantum fidelity of the corresponding single-particle reduced states from correlation measurements on ground-state ensembles of suitably engineered spin models. For a number of other models, we obtain not necessarily tight lower bounds. We also present bounds for various levels of multiparticle entanglement.
item.dc:creator: G\'eza T\'oth, J\'ozsef Pitrik

item.title: Vector alignment in matrix Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.30868v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many measurements in physics determine a linear transformation from pairs of input and output vectors, where the transformation is known in advance to belong to a matrix Lie group, for example the Lorentz group for the four-momenta measured by two inertial observers, or the unitary group for the states produced by a quantum circuit. Among the classical groups, only the rotation and unitary groups have a well-known closed form solution, given by the Kabsch and Horn algorithms and by the polar decomposition. We extend our previously proposed Lie algebra method from the image of the matrix exponential to the entire Lie group. We derive the projection in closed form for the classical groups over the real and complex numbers, including the indefinite orthogonal and unitary, symplectic, spin, special Euclidean and similarity groups, and we give conditions under which the method is exact for noiseless data, with examples in which it fails otherwise and an extension by a data dependent involution which is exact on the whole group. For noisy data, we bound the error of the method to first order in the noise, and we show that, for the orthogonal and unitary groups, it agrees with the least squares solution over the group to first order when the input vectors are isotropic, but not otherwise. We apply the method to an eight-qubit quantum circuit and to the rigid registration of point clouds, and compare it with Gauss--Newton refinement and direct minimization. A Julia implementation is provided.
item.dc:creator: Congzhou M Sha

item.title: A Topological Formula for Potts Lattice Gauge Theory Correlations
item.description: arXiv:2607.02434v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We exhibit a formula relating the correlation between Wilson loop variables in Potts lattice gauge theory to a topological quantity in the plaquette random cluster model. As applications we prove exponential decay of correlations between slowly growing Wilson loop variables for Ising lattice gauge theory on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ at all but the critical temperature, we demonstrate that the correlation length is finite at sufficiently high or low temperatures in any dimension, and we show that the correlation length of the model on $\mathbb{Z}^4$ with free boundary conditions equals that of the dual model with constant boundary conditions when $q$ is prime.
item.dc:creator: Paul Duncan, Benjamin Schweinhart

item.title: BRST quantization of Carroll-Weyl gauged null strings
item.description: arXiv:2608.02731v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the BRST quantization of the null string after completing its local gauge symmetry by Carroll-Weyl transformations. The resulting worldsheet theory possesses three first-class constraints, $C_1 = P^2$, $C_2 = P \cdot X'$, and $C_3 = P \cdot X$, whose modes realize a Weyl-BMS algebra. The additional Carroll-Weyl constraint qualitatively changes the quantum gauge complex: its scalar $s$-ghost is intrinsically coupled to the BMS $bc$-ghost sector, and the anomaly analysis involves three independent cocycles rather than a single Virasoro-type central charge. Starting from the gauge-fixed action, we derive the complete Faddeev-Popov complex, construct the matter and ghost currents and the BRST charge, and evaluate their equal-time operator products in the flipped, equivalently highest-weight, representation. The matter and ghost anomaly coefficients are $(c_{LL},c_{LS},c_{SS})_{\mathrm{matter}}=(2D,-D,-D)$ and $(c_{LL},c_{LS},c_{SS})_{\mathrm{ghost}}=(-54,6,4)$. Because the corresponding central terms multiply linearly independent ghost bilinears in $Q_B^2$, BRST nilpotency requires the three conditions $D=27$, $D=6$, and $D=4$, respectively. These conditions are mutually incompatible. Consequently, there is no target-space dimension in which the minimal flat Carroll-Weyl matter-plus-ghost complex is anomaly-free in the highest-weight representation. The familiar $D=26$ condition of the ILST null string is recovered only after truncation to the two-constraint BMS subsector, which defines a different quantum gauge complex.
item.dc:creator: Sarthak Duary, Sourav Maji

item.title: Elliptic solutions to matrix CKP equation
item.description: arXiv:2608.08774v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A class of elliptic solutions to the matrix CKP equation is studied. Equations of motion for their poles and matrix coefficients at the poles are obtained. As in the scalar case, they are of the first order, in contrast to what takes place in the KP and BKP hierarchies, where the equations of motion are of the second order.
item.dc:creator: A. Zabrodin

item.title: Inverse Semiclassical Scattering at Fixed Energy
item.description: arXiv:2609.02175v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate inverse scattering at a fixed energy for semiclassical Schr\"odinger operators with smooth potentials. For compactly supported potentials satisfying a natural virial condition, we prove that, under the sharp condition, $\liminf_{h\to0}\|S_1(\lambda,h)-S_2(\lambda,h)\|<2$ implies $V_1=V_2$, provided the fixed energy $\lambda$ lies above both potentials. We then consider radial short-range repulsive potentials. Under a monotonicity assumption on the radial force, we show that the semiclassical differential cross section at a fixed energy, up to $o(1)$ as $h\to0$, determines the potential in the classically accessible region. Finally, we obtain an analogous rigidity result for nontrapping compactly supported perturbations of the Euclidean metric under a strict convexity assumption.
item.dc:creator: Fran\c{c}ois Nicoleau

item.title: Non-simple blow-up for the Chern--Simons--Higgs equation on Riemannian surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.20042v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The existence and structure of non-simple blow-up are fundamental questions for the self-dual Chern--Simons--Higgs equation. Physically, this phenomenon describes magnetic-flux concentration in several cores whose mutual distances are much larger than their widths, although all cores approach the same vortex point. Despite substantial progress for singular Liouville equations, the existence of non-simple blow-up solutions to the full Chern--Simons--Higgs equation on closed surfaces has remained open in both the Chern--Simons (CS) and mean-field regimes. We prove that the cores of every non-simple cluster have equal limiting masses, share a common profile type, and form an asymptotically regular polygon. These identities yield an explicit finite list of admissible cluster masses and a four-unit mass-gap criterion. We also construct non-simple blow-up solutions on closed Riemannian surfaces in both regimes. Together, these results establish a sharp arithmetic criterion for single-point non-simple CS blow-up on each fixed flat torus when a suitable exterior divisor may be chosen, and show that vortex blow-up need not be simple, answering Li--Liu's question in the negative.
item.dc:creator: Youngae Lee, Lei Zhang

item.title: Lee-Yang theorem for fermions
item.description: arXiv:2609.23942v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Lee-Yang theorems are a powerful tool for studying many-body systems, with applications ranging from analyzing phase transitions to proving the efficiency of certain classical and quantum algorithms. In this work, we prove a Lee-Yang zero-freeness theorem for the partition function of a broad class of interacting fermion models, implying the existence of a provably efficient quantum algorithm for estimating their ground-state energies. This class includes several well-known models such as the attractive Hubbard model, repulsive Hubbard model on bipartite graphs, and the interacting Hofstadter model. Our results also rigorously establish the nonexistence of phase transitions in these models in the presence of a nonzero local external field.
item.dc:creator: Chaithanya Rayudu, Takahiro Misawa, Andrew Zhao, Jun Takahashi

item.title: Anti-successors and anti-replicators, Manin products and Koszul duality
item.description: arXiv:2610.21365v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop an operadic theory of anti-splitting and anti-replicating for binary operads. For a binary operad $\opd$, we define its anti-bisuccessor $\ABSu(\opd)$ and anti-trisuccessor $\ATSu(\opd)$. Each generating operation is recovered as the negative sum of two or three split operations, yielding canonical operad morphisms $\opd\to\ABSu(\opd)$ and $\opd\to\ATSu(\opd)$. For binary quadratic operads, these constructions are described by Manin black products: \[ \ABSu(\opd)\cong\antiprelie\bullet\opd, \qquad \ATSu(\opd)\cong\antipostlie\bullet\opd. \] Dually, we also introduce the canonical quadratic anti-duplicator and anti-triplicator, together with their combinatorial counterparts defined by labeled planar binary trees. We show that they coincide precisely under a full-support condition. As applications, we obtain anti-dupli-com and anti-dupli-Lie algebras. We also display an example in which the two constructions differ. Furthermore, we establish the Koszul duality relations \[ \widehat{\ADup}(\opd^!) \cong\ABSu(\opd)^!, \qquad \widehat{\ATrip}(\opd^!) \cong\ATSu(\opd)^!, \] providing an effective description of the canonical quadratic anti-duplicator in terms of the Manin white product. The framework recovers known constructions, including anti-dendriform, anti-pre-Lie and anti-pre-Poisson algebras, and produces further examples and Koszul dual pairs.
item.dc:creator: Chengming Bai, Li Guo, Yunhe Sheng, You Wang

item.title: The symplectic leaves of the affine Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme associated with a singular subalgebroid
item.description: arXiv:2610.30395v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Every singular subalgebroid, and in particular every singular foliation $\mathscr{G}$, determines a universal Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$, which is the analogue of the linear Poisson structure on the dual of a Lie algebroid. We show that the underlying space $X_{\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G})}$ of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$ decomposes as a disjoint union of symplectic manifolds. Furthermore, we extend the Helffer-Nourrigat cone to a singular subalgebroid and show that it is an embedded Poisson $C^\infty$-subscheme of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$.
item.dc:creator: Ruben Louis

item.title: Classifying Leibniz racks
item.description: arXiv:2610.35534v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Lie quandles were defined by T. Fritz as a nonlinear generalization of Lie algebras, to serve as a nonlinear algebras of observables in generalized form of Hamiltonian mechanics. These objects were subsequently generalized in a prequel article to objects referred to as smooth Lie group families of smooth racks by the authors. In this article, we investigate a particular system of nonlinear functional differential equations whose solution in general provides a pathway to the classification of smooth Lie group families of smooth rack structures on any given smooth manifold. We then discuss a particularly practical ansatz for solving these equations, and use it to construct new families of examples, as well as prove a result on the sense in which the Bloch sphere is the unique Lie quandle structure on the sphere.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Elhamdadi, Bryce Virgin

item.title: Quantum communication: a discrimination approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.40358v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a state discrimination approach to unassisted quantum communication through a noisy quantum channel. Starting from the operational duality between entanglement recovery and state discrimination, we construct entanglement-generation codes with explicit decoders constructed from Petz recovery maps. The resulting error bounds hold for every number of channel uses and are expressed in terms of Petz-R\'enyi coherent information. For product sources, they yield exponential error decay at rates below coherent information.
item.dc:creator: Hao-Chung Cheng

item.title: Galois-modular obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.04232v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article we establish new obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings by combining the values of irreducible characters of the Grothendieck ring with the Galois symmetry of the induced unit object $I(1)$ in the Drinfeld center. As a result, we show that a near-group ring of type $G+m$, where $G$ is an abelian group and both $|G|$ and $m$ are odd, can only categorify if $m=|G|$.
item.dc:creator: V\'ictor Blasco
